title: AMM withdraw slippage anchored to vault internal rate bricks exits during AMM discount
downgradeReason: DoS-on-withdraw maps to 'protocol availability impacted' = Medium. The sandwich-extraction framing is structurally weak - the vault-anchored minOut is conservative, so manipulated swaps revert rather than executing at unfavorable rates.

classification.assetImpact: Withdrawals can be DoS'd entirely when the AMM trades at a discount to the vault rate. Protocol availability for honest clients is impacted whenever the strategy's intended use case (AMM/vault rate divergence on sUSDe-style assets) actually occurs.
attackPath: 1. Strategy uses vault.convertToAssets/convertToShares as the anchor for minOut on every Curve swap.
2. The vault rate is a slow-moving accumulator and does not reflect transient AMM price impact or the AMM market price.

3. When the AMM trades at a discount to the vault rate (the exact market condition the strategy was designed to handle), the vault-anchored minOut is unreachable and all client withdrawals revert (DoS).
4. Clients have no self-service exit; the only escape is the owner-only emergencyWithdraw which routes shares to the owner rather than returning underlying to the client.
classification.likelihood: medium - AMM/vault-rate divergence is a normal market condition for sUSDe-style assets but does not directly enable theft
classification.assumptions: AMM trades at a discount larger than slippageToleranceBps relative to the vault internal rate

justification: Protocol availability is impacted: clients are DoS'd from withdrawing exactly during the market condition the strategy is advertised to handle. No direct theft path because the conservative vault-anchored minOut causes manipulated swaps to revert rather than execute at unfavorable rates.
